title: Slow Cooker Teriyaki London Broil

items: 2–3 lb top round London broil, about 1½–2 inches thick
¼ cup mirin (or 3 Tbsp rice vinegar plus 1 Tbsp sugar)
¼ cup sake (or dry sherry, dry white wine or more broth)
¼ cup beef broth or water
1 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 Tbsp cold water
Red pepper flakes or sriracha, to taste, optional

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, broth and sesame oil in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Pat the beef dry and season with pepper. Skip salt, since the soy brings plenty. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then sear 2–3 min per side and a few seconds on the edges, until deeply browned.
Pour about ¼ cup of the sauce into the hot pan and scrape up the browned bits for 30 seconds. Pour it into the slow cooker.
Put the beef in the slow cooker and pour the rest of the sauce over it. Cover and cook on low 4½–5 hr, flipping once halfway if you can.

Check it at 4 hr the first time, since slow cookers vary. It's ready when a fork goes in with slight resistance and the meat holds together when lifted. If it feels tight and springy, give it 30 min more.
Move the beef to a cutting board, tent with foil and rest 10–15 min.
Meanwhile, strain the liquid into a small saucepan and skim off the fat. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and stir 2–3 min, until glossy and it coats a spoon.
Slice across the grain ⅛–¼ inch thick, at a slight angle. Fan the slices on a platter, spoon the glaze over them and top with green onions and sesame seeds. Serve the extra sauce on the side.
tips: For more flavor, marinate the beef in half the sauce in a zip-top bag in the fridge 2–8 hr (no more than 12). Wipe off the marinade before searing so the sugar doesn't burn.
Slicing thin across the grain matters more than anything else for tender top round. If it's tough, slice thinner or give it 30–60 min more next time.
Serve with white or jasmine rice and steamed broccoli, snap peas or bok choy. Leftovers make good rice bowls or teriyaki beef sandwiches.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the slices stored in the sauce so they don't dry out. Freezer up to 3 months, sliced, in sauce. Reheat gently in a covered skillet with a splash of water; full-power microwaving makes lean beef rubbery.
